text:
maya: quick note 01 the JS quickstart shows a browser fetch example that sets `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY` in client-side code. New users copy/paste and leak keys in frontend.

luke: yikes. where is that exactly?

maya: in docs/quickstarts/js.md under the "Browser example" section. snippet looks like:
```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'Authorization': 'Bearer YOUR_KEY' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'Hello' })
});
```

rachel: we intentionally had a server-side example too but it's buried. agree we should remove direct browser auth and add a clear warning and a server-proxy snippet or `@redwood/inference` usage.

luke: suggested replacement: short note + server example: "Do not put API keys in client code. Use a server endpoint that calls Redwood and returns only the generated text." and show a minimal Express example.

maya: also add a one-line security callout at top of quickstart and update the code sample. we should run a docs grep to find any other browser auth examples.

docs-bot: scanning repo for "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY"... found matches in `docs/quickstarts/js.md` and `examples/browser-chat/README.md`. I'll file PR comments on the open quickstart PR.

support-bot: flagged 2 support tickets where users accidentally published keys after following the quickstart. recommended next steps: patch docs ASAP, update website quickstart, and send a short security note to onboarding docs.

rachel: i'll open a small PR to replace the browser snippet with a secure server proxy example and add the security callout. i'll also add a short CI check: a regex scan in docs workflow to detect "Authorization: Bearer" in markdown and fail the job.

luke: love the regex scan idea. make it optional until we fix everything. ping me when PR is up and i'll review. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all. small but important DX/security fix.
